title: Radius Certificate
$comment: One `reports/radius/<cert_id>.cert.json` of DESIGN-retraction-closure §4: the receipt a retraction carries. Generated by the radius tool from a pinned graph and a single root; never hand-edited, never partially published. Committed BEFORE the tool exists (v0.16 preregistration) so that the certificate's shape — and in particular the two fields the design added against its own interest, `unprovenanced_nodes` and `inferred_edges_excluded` — cannot be dropped once they turn out to be embarrassing. Every field is required: a certificate that omits its unprovenanced remainder would report a smaller radius than it computed.

cert_id.$comment: Also the filename stem under reports/radius/. One root, one certificate; a re-run after any graph edit is a new preregistration and therefore a new cert_id, never an overwrite (design §6, R2).

root_node.$comment: The node whose falsification is being priced. It must exist in the graph identified by graph_sha256, and it is a member of its own closure.

root_falsification_kind.$comment: Why the root is being treated as wrong. `ledger_stale` is the kind the first slice actually exercises: the two live drifts on main are the tool's first real work (design §3, §5).

closure.$comment: Every node reachable backward-consequence-wise from the root over emitted (inferred: false) edges only. The design never claims this set is SUFFICIENT — repairing it is not certified to restore correctness — and absence from it is never a negative certificate (design §7).

closure_size.$comment: Must equal len(closure). JSON Schema cannot express that equality; the recheck script enforces it structurally, and it is written out anyway because R2's ratio clause (closure_size <= 3 x |ground truth|) is read off the certificate rather than recomputed by the reader.

depth_histogram.$comment: Backward depth from the root to count of closure members at that depth. Keys are decimal integers as strings because JSON object keys are strings; depth 0 is the root itself, so its count is always 1.

unprovenanced_nodes.$comment: Claims with no machine-locatable anchor, or nodes with incomplete inbound edges, that this closure touched. Listed on EVERY certificate that touches them (R3) — the design forbids silent omission, because an unlisted remainder is indistinguishable from a clean closure.

inferred_edges_excluded.$comment: edge_id of every inferred (reconstructed) edge that would have entered this closure had it been scored. Published so the reader can see the size of what the gate refuses to count, not to be counted.

graph_sha256.$comment: Pins the exact reports/provenance_graph.jsonl this closure was derived from. R5 requires two clean builds to reproduce it byte-identically, or every certificate in the cycle is void.

recheck_command.$comment: The literal command that re-derives this closure from (graph, root). R4 bounds it at 600 seconds on the declared host, and the re-derived closure must hash equal.

standing_limitation.const: This graph records data lineage, not conceptual dependency; a convention shared by many artifacts and an input to none is outside it. See DESIGN-retraction-closure section 7.
standing_limitation.$comment: A const, not a free string: both historical retractions were exactly this shape, and a certificate that could reword or soften its own limitation would repeat the failure the design exists to end.

gate.$comment: Design §6's frozen construction-gate numbers, carried as consts inside the schema that the certificates validate against so the gate travels with the artifact rather than only with the prose. This block validates nothing at publish time and is referenced by no property; it is the machine-readable copy of the numbers, and the preregistration test asserts these exact values. Moving one of them fails that test rather than quietly moving the gate.

r1_emitted_edge_fraction.$comment: R1 - writers emit their own edges: at least this fraction of edges into report_ledger and ledger_section nodes carry inferred: false.

r2_closure_to_ground_truth_ratio.$comment: R2 - the live drifts are explained, superset-exactly: closure_size <= 3 x |pre-committed hand-audited ground truth|, and the closure must be a superset. One missed claim voids the capability.

r3_anchored_claims_floor.$comment: R3 - coverage floor: at least this fraction of the current release's claims resolve to anchored nodes with complete inbound edges; the remainder appear in unprovenanced_nodes.

r4_recheck_seconds.$comment: R4 - independent recheck: the recheck_command re-derives every published closure within this many seconds on the declared host, hashes matching.

r5_identical_builds.$comment: R5 - byte reproducibility: this many clean builds must reproduce graph_sha256 byte-identically, or every certificate in the cycle is void.

blind_shuffle_count.$comment: The blind control: this many degree-preserving, kind-preserving edge shuffles, seeds committed in advance at data/retraction_closure/shuffle_seeds.json, each run against both live drift roots. If one or more satisfies R2 on both roots, the real edges carry no consequence-relevant information and the capability is void.
